newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent briefly dips below $23.70 on US selling.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent briefly dips below $23.70 on US selling.

text.p: IPE Brent futures briefly dipped below $23.70 a barrel under selling pressure from U.S. funds on Thursday afternoon but quickly recovered.
December Brent was down 34 cents at $23.73 a barrel at 1430 GMT, up from the day's low of $23.65 set shortly before.
"There's no fresh news affecting the market but if Brent stays below $23.70 it could be dire. The U.S. is pushing it lower," said Tim Holmes of brokers MeesPierson Derivatives in London.

Despite sharp losses this week many traders are relaxed above the move which has bucked a three-month uptrend. They expected a corrective move lower after Brent's relentless climb of about $5.00 a barrel since July.
"It's barely paused for breath recently, so we would expect a period of profit taking," said a Rotterdam-based trader.
Gas oil futures remained the weakest area of the market with November down $5.75 a tonne at $220.00 at 1420 GMT.
"It's gas oil's and heat's fall which has pulled the market off," one trader said.

"At this time of year gas oil's strength is very much connected with the weather situation, whereas over the last months it has been related to stock building," said another trade."The fine weather across most of Europe is taking its toll."
